body.statement:
Suppose \(0<c\leq 1\), \(N/T\to c\), and \(Z_{NT}=E/(\sigma\sqrt T)\).  Let \(P_{NT}\) be deterministic of fixed rank, independent of \(Z_{NT}\), and suppose its largest singular value converges to \(s\).  Then
\[
s_1(Z_{NT}+P_{NT})^2\longrightarrow
\begin{cases}
(1+\sqrt c)^2,&s\leq c^{1/4},\\
s^2+1+c+c/s^2,&s>c^{1/4},
\end{cases}
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 2.8 (Largest singular value phase transition). For each fixed 1 ≤ i ≤ r, the i-th singular value converges almost surely to D_muX^{-1}(1/theta_i^2) if theta_i exceeds the threshold, and to b otherwise. In Section 3.1, for an n × m Gaussian matrix with independent zero-mean entries of variance 1/m and n/m → c ∈ (0,1], equation (9) gives, for any deterministic fixed-rank P_n, sigma_i(X_n+P_n) → sqrt((1+theta_i^2)(c+theta_i^2)/theta_i^2) when i ≤ r and theta_i > c^(1/4), and 1+sqrt(c) otherwise.

attestation.note: Primary-source verification from arXiv:1103.2221v2 PDF downloaded directly from https://arxiv.org/pdf/1103.2221 on 2026-09-16; checked Assumptions 2.1, 2.3, 2.4, Theorem 2.8, and Section 3.1 equation (9). The paper explicitly specializes to deterministic fixed-rank perturbations in the Gaussian example.
